text:
Maya: Quick flag — TrellisPay usage cratered this week, procurement is running an RFP with SkyServe. Renewal in ~6 weeks. Champion (Elena) is worried about costs. Need quick retention play.

Elena: Hey team, sorry for radio silence. CTO left last week, procurement looped in a new lead (Sam). They're asking for a cost/latency comparison ASAP. We're evaluating cheaper quantized stacks on SkyServe.

Raj: How bad is the drop? API calls or sessions?

Elena: API tokens down ~40% vs last 30d, active sessions down from 115 -> 68. Embeds specifically took the biggest hit.

Diego: I'll run a prefix/top-route breakdown and send a heatmap. SQL I used:```sql
SELECT prefix, sum(tokens) as tokens, count(*) as calls
FROM api_events
WHERE acct='TRE-001' AND day >= current_date - interval '30 days'
GROUP BY prefix
ORDER BY tokens DESC
LIMIT 50;
```

Lin: Procurement will want: p50/p95 latency, $/token breakdown with current reserved nodes vs a SkyServe estimate, and an ops checklist showing quick wins (caching/batching/quant). I can draft a one-pager.

Nora: Commercial options: discounts need legal signoff, but we can offer a short-term retention credit. Proposal idea: 10% credit on overages for 90 days + a joint technical enablement with eng. Legal ETA EOD.

Maya: Good. Action list: Diego sends heatmap + chart (ETA 1h); Lin drafts procurement one-pager (ETA today 5pm PT); Nora confirms credit terms (ETA EOD); Maya schedules 30m intro with Sam + Elena (ETA 2h).

renewal-bot: Account TRE-001 health: 78 -> 59 in 7d. Renewal window: 44 days. Recommended workflow: "at-risk - engage commercial + tech".

Raj: Also surface any 429/5xx spikes that could explain user friction. Even client-side batching changes can cause 429s and drop perceived reliability.

Diego: Quick check: no 5xx spike last 30d. Embedding route 429s increased around 2026-02-10 which lines up with a batch-size change we saw in their user-agent string. I'll include a timeline.

Elena: Sam (procurement) prioritizes cost but cares about business continuity. He requested an RFP deck by Thursday EOD.

Lin: For comparison, I'll create a simple TCO calc: current committed 3 nodes (A100-ish) = $X/day (estimated). SkyServe quantized estimate = current * 0.75 (ballpark). I'll include sensitivity to batch size and prefix caching.

Maya: Diego, can you run a simulation that shows tokens saved if we enable prefix caching + KV for top 10 prefixes? Even a conservative 10% token reduction could matter.

Diego: On it. I'll run a sim and attach CSV + chart.

Nora: If they sign a 6-month extension before renewal we can offer a 12% overage credit for Q2. If they prefer no extension, we can do a 6% one-off credit. I'll try to get both options in writing.

Maya: Let's plan the enablement call invite: attendees: Sam (procurement), Elena (champion), Maya, Lin (cost), Diego (ops demo), Nora (commercial). Proposed slots: tomorrow 9:00am PT or 4:00pm PT.

Elena: 4pm PT works best for Sam. Please send calendar.

Raj: Also prepare a short FAQ: common SkyServe tradeoffs (latency variance, maintenance, model freshness). We should highlight our unified support and rollback policies.

Lin: Draft bullets: - We support model pinning and rollbacks; - KV/prefix caching built-in; - Transparent per-route P95 + token billing; - Can run a short PoC on dedicated pool to mirror their production traffic.

Maya: Perfect. Once deck looks good, let's do a 20m dry-run internally.

renewal-bot: Note: last contact with champion 2026-02-28 was positive. Risk score bumped to high due to CTO departure and RFP.

Diego: Charts here: https://redwood.internal/snapshots/TRE-001/prefix-heatmap-1806667890.png and timeline CSV will be uploaded to the share.

Nora: Legal approved draft language for credit offering (sending link).

Maya: I'll send the invite for 4pm PT and attach Lin's one-pager when ready. Thanks team. :pray:

Elena: Thanks y'all, appreciate the quick turnaround.

Maya: Follow-ups: Diego post CSV; Lin share slide draft here; Nora confirm final credit wording; Maya run dry-run after internal review.

Raj: Keep this thread updated — procurement moves fast once RFP docs land.

Maya: Will do.
